title: Test scenarios
description: One file per endpoint (API) or feature (UI) in <layer>/<area>/: a suite of scenarios. Key order inside a scenario: id, name, ref, tags, status, automatedIn, role, knownIssue, bug, preconditions, steps.

tags.description: Tags for the whole suite: @<area> for UI (@cart), @<area>-api for API (@products-api). The spec's test.describe is titled '<tags joined by spaces> - <suite>'.

id.description: Unique scenario ID: <PREFIX>-<number>, numbered across the layer, with the prefix and digits from simpright.yml (ids.layers), e.g. API-0001 or UI-001. The test title starts with it.

name.description: Scenario name (the test title after the ID).

ref.description: Optional link to what the scenario comes from: a user story, bug or document (US-123, BUG-001, docs/ui/user-stories/Product_Detail.md#AC3), or a list of them.

tags.description: Optional tags of this scenario's test, on top of the suite's: @smoke puts it in the smoke set (fast, reliable happy paths; automated, no knownIssue, only writes it cleans up). The test carries them as Playwright's tag option: test('<ID>: <name>', { tag: '@smoke' }, ...).

status.description: manual (the default for a new scenario) or automated (set together with automatedIn when a spec automates it).

automatedIn.description: Path of the spec that automates this scenario. Required when status is automated, absent when it's manual.

role.description: Role of the test, one of the profile's roles. Absent means the default user; guest means logged out.

knownIssue.description: How this scenario hits a known app bug: one sentence naming the wrong behaviour and the expected one. Needs bug; becomes the test's 'Known issue <bug>: <text>' annotation.

bug.description: The open bug (bugs/<ID>.yml) behind knownIssue, e.g. BUG-001; set together with knownIssue. Scenarios that hit the same root cause name the same bug.

preconditions.description: The state the test starts from, set up by a precondition fixture or setup code before the steps, not by a test step: the page that is open, the logged-in customer, the cart's contents, data created through the API. Each one is a statement, e.g. 'The home page is open.'.

steps.description: Ordered steps. Checks are steps that start with 'Verify'.
